title: Labor induction
what: If labor does not start on its own, the doctor helps it start. First the cervix is softened, then contractions are started if needed.
why: For an overdue pregnancy, waters breaking without contractions, high blood pressure, diabetes, and other reasons when waiting is riskier.
duration: from a few hours to 1 to 3 days, depending on how ready the cervix is
tell_doctor: A past C-section or uterine surgery
If your waters have broken, and when
Your fears and wishes. Your doctor will explain each step

prepare.title: Your decision
prepare.text: Your doctor will explain why induction is needed and what the options are. You sign a consent form.

prepare.title: Bag
prepare.text: Bring your hospital bag. The process can take a few days.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can usually have a light meal before induction. Check with the maternity unit.

steps: The doctor examines your cervix and decides where to start
Usually a gel or tablet is placed in the vagina first, or you take a tablet by mouth
Sometimes a small balloon is placed in the cervix to open it gently
After a few hours, the doctor examines you again
If needed, the waters are broken. It does not hurt
Sometimes a drip with medicine that strengthens contractions is started
Your baby's heartbeat is watched the whole time
feel: The exam and balloon placement are unpleasant
Induced contractions can be stronger. You can ask for pain relief
after: From there, labor goes as usual
If induction does not work, your doctor will discuss other options with you, including a C-section
red_flags: Severe constant belly pain or bleeding: tell the staff right away
Your baby is moving much less: tell the staff

faq.q: Is an induced labor more painful?
faq.a: Sometimes contractions are stronger. Pain relief is available just as in a regular labor.
It varies: from a few hours to 1 to 3 days. The softer the cervix, the faster.
Yes. Your doctor will explain the risks of waiting in your case, and you will decide together.

reminders.text: Labor induction tomorrow. Pack your hospital bag, documents, and pregnancy record.
